content.text:
I'm going to stop here. My eyes hurt and I'm not going to scroll any further.

**Screen 1**
- The top says "איפה ואיך הכי זול להשקיע במדד, לאורך זמן". To me "מדד" is the price index from the news. They mean something else here.
- There's a row of buttons with English letters: "S&P 500", "MSCI World", "נאסד"ק 100". S… and… P. The 500 one is lit up, so I suppose that's the one they gave me.
- It says "מדד של חמש מאות החברות הגדולות בארצות הברית… הכסף מושקע בדולרים". So these are American shares, in dollars. That isn't a deposit.
- There are sliders with boxes: "סכום היום 10,000", "הפקדה חודשית 500", "10 שנים", "7%". I'm not touching the sliders.
- Big number: "הפקדתם 70,000 ₪". Next to it, in a box: "86,492 ₪ … נשאר לכם בעוד 10 שנים, אחרי דמי ניהול ומס". That's the number that stays with me. But it rests on the 7% they wrote in. Nobody promises me 7%.
- The box says "הבחירה שלכם · הזול ★". The company is "ילין לפידות מחקה S&P 500 (4D)" and the account is "פסגות ניירות ערך". I don't know Yalin Lapidot. Psagot I've heard of, but it isn't my bank.
- I looked at the long coloured bars and the little coloured dots and gave up. I can't tell the colours apart.
- It says "דמי ניהול: 0.02%". That sounds like very little, but I don't know if it's per year or what.

**Screen 2**
- On the left is a long list, every line in English: "iShares", "Vanguard", "UCITS ETF", "Accumulating". Down the side, in red: "−213", "−447", "−1,268", "−4,492". Red and minus signs. I don't want any of those.
- A dark grey box lay on top of the list ("מס רק במכירה…"). I couldn't read it.
- On the right were names I know: "לאומי", "הבינלאומי", "הפועלים", "מזרחי טפחות". Psagot is at the top with "1,057 ₪". Leumi has "4,541 ₪" and Mizrahi "10,608 ₪". Under Psagot the first screen said "מה החשבון גובה ב־10 שנים: 1,057". So I think the small number is what the place takes over ten years. If that's right, the banks take a lot more.
- Some banks had a red bar. That made me nervous.

---

**What I'd tell my son:**
"I didn't decide anything, and I'm certainly not putting money in. As far as I understood, the cheapest choice they showed is a fund called Yalin Lapidot, held in an account at Psagot. On their numbers, 70,000 ₪ becomes about 86,000 in ten years. Through Leumi or Mizrahi you'd pay the bank thousands more. That surprised me. But it's American shares, in dollars, and it's not a deposit. Half the screen was English letters and red minuses, so I stopped after two screens. Come over and look at it with me. And ask why the banks take four or ten times as much."
